title: Right-fibration mapping spaces, restrictions and fiberwise equivalences
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and right fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Fix an arbitrary small simplicial set $S$. For any map $a:Z\to S$ and any right fibration $q:Y\to S$, define $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)_m$ to be the maps $Z\times\Delta^m\to Y$ whose composite with $q$ is $a\operatorname{pr}_Z$, with simplex operators by precomposition. This is a Kan complex. For every monomorphism $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ over $S$, restriction
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(B,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,Y)$$
is a Kan fibration. In particular if $T\hookrightarrow S$ is a simplicial subset then restriction to the pullbacks over $T$ is a Kan fibration. If $f:X\to Y$ is a map over $S$ between right fibrations and each map of vertex fibers $f_s:X_s\to Y_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, then $f$ has an inverse up to simplicial homotopies over $S$: there is $g:Y\to X$ over $S$, and maps $X\times\Delta^1\to X$ and $Y\times\Delta^1\to Y$ over $S$ with endpoints $(gf,1_X)$ and $(fg,1_Y)$. No quasicategory hypothesis on $S$ and no model structure on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$ is assumed.

proof.text: First record how to solve a lifting problem for a right fibration $q:E\to S$ against a right anodyne inclusion $u:C\hookrightarrow D$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $q$ and $u$. Its displayed restriction/postcomposition map is a trivial Kan fibration, hence surjective on vertices by [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. A vertex of its target is exactly a compatible pair $C\to E$, $D\to S$; a preimage is the required extension $D\to E$. Thus every such right-anodyne lifting problem has a solution, without any assumption on $S$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, right-handed assertion, and the dimension-zero boundary lifting condition.

proof.text:
Write $M_q(Z)=\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,E)$, with simplices and operators as in the statement and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Given a monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$ over $S$, a lifting problem for $M_q(B)\to M_q(A)$ against a right horn $\Lambda_j^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ ($0<j\leq n$) is, by evaluating the maps, precisely a lifting problem for $q$ with source inclusion
$$(\Lambda_j^n\times B)\cup_{\Lambda_j^n\times A}(\Delta^n\times A)\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times B.$$
The map to $S$ is the structure map of $B$ composed with projection. The horn is right anodyne, and [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] makes the displayed inclusion right anodyne. Step 1 fills it; hence the restriction is a right fibration in the horn sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Taking $A=\varnothing$ proves that $M_q(B)\to\Delta^0$ is a right fibration. The point is Kan, so [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] shows $M_q(B)$ is Kan. The same argument applies to $A$, and a second application of that node to the restriction, whose target $M_q(A)$ is now Kan, makes the restriction a Kan fibration. For $T\hookrightarrow S$ take $A=Z\times_ST\hookrightarrow B=Z$: maps from $A\times\Delta^m$ to $E$ over $S$ factor uniquely through $E\times_ST$, degree by degree. Thus its target is exactly the mapping simplicial set over $T$ asserted in the subset clause.

proof.text: For the last assertion, write $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$ and $qf=p$. Define a simplicial set $P$ as follows. An $n$-simplex is a pair $(x,h)$, where $x:\Delta^n\to X$ and $h:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to Y$ satisfy $h|_{\Delta^n\times\{0\}}=fx$ and $qh=px\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^n}$. Operators restrict $x$ and the $\Delta^n$ coordinate of $h$. Put $e(x,h)=x$, $r(x,h)=h|_{\Delta^n\times\{1\}}$, and let $c:X\to P$ send $x$ to $(x,fx\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^n})$. These formulas commute with all operators and give $ec=1_X$, $rc=f$, and $pe=qr$. Evaluation is a simplicial map $P\times\Delta^1\to Y$, is over $S$, and has endpoints $(fe,r)$. These are direct substitutions in the degreewise products and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; the structure maps and fibers use [def-coef-infinity-fibrations].

source.place: Agent mapping-path construction for the implication (a) to (b) of Lemma 2.2.3.6; formulas given here, rather than attributed to its skeletal proof.

proof.text:
The endpoint map $r:P\to Y$ is a right fibration. Fix $n\geq1$, $0<j\leq n$, a map $\Lambda_j^n\to P$ and a simplex $y:\Delta^n\to Y$ agreeing after $r$. The first coordinate of the horn is a map to $X$ over the restriction of $qy$. Since $p$ is a right fibration as defined in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], extend this coordinate to $x:\Delta^n\to X$ with $px=qy$. The given horn homotopy and the two maps $fx,y$ on the endpoints agree on their intersections and define a map to $Y$ on
$$(\Lambda_j^n\times\Delta^1)\cup_{\Lambda_j^n\times\partial\Delta^1}(\Delta^n\times\partial\Delta^1).$$
Here $\partial\Delta^1=\{0\}\amalg\{1\}$. Its inclusion into $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied to the right horn and the endpoint monomorphism. Its map to $S$ is $qy\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^n}$. Step 1, using [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] and vertex surjectivity in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], extends the homotopy over all of this product. Together with $x$ it is a filler in $P$ whose endpoint is exactly $y$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3 and Proposition 4.2.5.4 (0154); agent application to the mapping-path endpoint projection.

proof.text:
Fix a vertex $y$ of $Y$ and put $s=q(y)$. Pullback preserves the right-horn lifting property: a horn lifting problem in a pullback is the same problem in the original map with the prescribed base map. Consequently $X_s\to\Delta^0$ and $Y_s\to\Delta^0$ are right fibrations, and [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes $X_s,Y_s$ Kan. From the formulas of step 3 there is a degreewise identification
$$P_y=X_s\times_{Y_s,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Y_s)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Y_s}\{y\}=\operatorname{hofib}_y(f_s).$$
This is exactly the homotopy fiber convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with fibers as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. By hypothesis $f_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Apply the mapping-path assertion of [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion]: the displayed fiber is weakly contractible and is a vertex fiber of a Kan fibration, hence Kan (lift horns with constant downstairs map). Step 4 supplies the right-fibration hypothesis on $r$. Thus [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers], applied with base $Y$, proves that $r:P\to Y$ is a trivial Kan fibration. This use permits an arbitrary base $Y$; it never assumes that $Y$ or $S$ is Kan.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.14, implication (3) to (1); Corollary 4.4.3.8 (01NV); mapping-path/homotopy-fiber statement of lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion, based on 00ZP.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to $r$ and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Y$, with lower map $1_Y$, to obtain a section $t:Y\to P$ with $rt=1_Y$. Set $g=et:Y\to X$. Since $pg=pet=qrt=q$, it is over $S$. The evaluation homotopy of step 3, precomposed with $t\times1_{\Delta^1}$, is $J:Y\times\Delta^1\to Y$ over $S$ with endpoints $(fet,rt)=(fg,1_Y)$. For the other composite the two maps $tf,c:X\to P$ satisfy $rtf=f=rc$. Their union is a map $X\times\partial\Delta^1\to P$, taking the first endpoint to $tf$ and the second to $c$. The endpoint inclusion $X\times\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow X\times\Delta^1$ is injective in every degree, and this union lies above the map $f\operatorname{pr}_X:X\times\Delta^1\to Y$. Apply the same monomorphism-lifting node to get $L:X\times\Delta^1\to P$ with $rL=f\operatorname{pr}_X$ and those endpoints. Then $H=eL$ has endpoints $(etf,ec)=(gf,1_X)$ and satisfies $pH=peL=qrL=qf\operatorname{pr}_X=p\operatorname{pr}_X$. This gives the required homotopy over $S$ in the specified direction, with no concatenation or reversal of homotopies required.

tool_uses.why: Generic horn-lifting fact: a right fibration over a Kan simplicial set is a Kan fibration. The current unit contains no such criterion; it is used only with Kan mapping-space targets or the point.
